evidence_sources.subject: anti-reflective optical coating

accepted_phrases: Anti-reflective coatings can reduce reflection and stray light, improving transmission and contrast, while performance depends on wavelength and angle. The mechanism does not establish which exact seller lens has the best coating or a visible output advantage.

evidence_sources.object: dispersion can produce color fringes, with axial and transverse forms behaving differently
evidence_sources.subject: chromatic aberration

accepted_phrases: Chromatic aberration occurs when colors do not share one focus or magnification and can appear as colored fringes at contrast boundaries. It must be measured by position, aperture and output rather than inferred from price or a product label.

evidence_sources.object: smaller apertures increase diffraction and at f/22 many modern lenses can be diffraction limited
evidence_sources.subject: diffraction limit

accepted_phrases: Diffraction sets a physical resolution limit and grows as the aperture is made smaller; at f/22 many modern lenses can be diffraction limited. Stopping down can reduce some aberrations yet eventually reduce detail, so aperture tests need the intended output.

evidence_sources.object: bright sources, optical interfaces and shading affect visible artifacts and contrast loss
evidence_sources.subject: lens flare

accepted_phrases: Lens flare comes from scattering or internal reflection and can create visible artifacts or washed-out contrast, especially with bright sources. It must be tested with declared light position and hood use, not inferred from element count, coating copy or price.

evidence_sources.object: the title names a NIKKOR Z MC 105mm f/2.8 VR S and calls the post the author's first picture with it
evidence_sources.subject: one first-picture macro-lens community post

accepted_phrases: One community title identifies a newly acquired NIKKOR Z 105mm macro lens and a first picture, without a same-scene before-and-after trial or relevant Canon compatibility. It cannot establish upgrade value, regret or a general optical cutoff.

evidence_sources.object: the title names only a 55-250mm lens and commenters still ask which camera and whether the image is a composite
evidence_sources.subject: one 55-250mm moon-image community post

accepted_phrases: One moon-image post identifies only a 55-250mm lens while commenters still ask which camera and whether it is a composite. The missing capture and processing details make it unsuitable as lens-only performance or price-cutoff evidence.

evidence_sources.object: contrast transfer varies with spatial frequency, focus and the full imaging chain
evidence_sources.subject: optical transfer function

accepted_phrases: OTF, and its commonly used magnitude MTF, describes how imaging contrast changes with spatial scale. It is not one context-free sharpness score and must be tied to focus, sensor, processing, display or print size and relevant detail.

evidence_sources.object: light capture, color, evenness, sharpness, flare, aberrations, weight, cost and mechanical operation are traded against sensor and use limits
evidence_sources.subject: photographic lens design

accepted_phrases: Photographic lens design balances acceptable rendition against cost, weight, materials, flare, aberrations and mechanical behavior, and maximum possible resolution may exceed the recording medium's needs. This rejects a one-dimensional price-to-sharpness cutoff.

evidence_sources.object: a prime is less versatile than a zoom and is often, but not automatically, faster, lighter or optically superior
evidence_sources.subject: prime lens category

accepted_phrases: A photographic prime is a fixed-focal-length lens; compared with a zoom it is less versatile and is often faster, lighter, smaller or optically better. Often is not always, and the category statement does not rank the exact 35mm, 40mm, 50mm and zoom offers.

evidence_sources.object: the effect can be stronger at short focal ratios and can be corrected with optical design choices
evidence_sources.subject: spherical aberration

accepted_phrases: Spherical aberration can make central and outer rays focus differently and may be more pronounced at fast focal ratios, while design can correct it. A wider f-number alone therefore neither guarantees nor disproves sharp output.

evidence_sources.object: it can arise from lens, settings, filters or hoods and can also be used intentionally
evidence_sources.subject: vignetting

accepted_phrases: Vignetting is peripheral brightness or saturation reduction and may come from settings, lens limitations, filters or hoods; it can also be intentional. It needs frame-position, aperture and accessory tests rather than a universal pass or fail.

generator_view.scenario: A Canon APS-C beginner bought a frozen EOS 4000D small kit with an EF-S 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6 III lens and now hears that lenses matter more than bodies. The intended outputs are ordinary web posts and small prints, and the real tasks are indoor family pictures, moving children, portraits, travel, landscape and backlit scenes. Six frozen seller pages span the 4000D kit at 464.99 dollars, a Canon EF 50mm f/1.8 STM import-model accessory bundle at 158.99 dollars, a Canon EF 40mm f/2.8 STM at 199.99 dollars, a renewed Sigma 35mm f/1.4 Art at 649.99 dollars, a Canon EF 35mm f/1.4L white-box bulk lens at 1098 dollars and a Canon EF 24-70mm f/4L IS zoom at 999 dollars. General sources describe anti-reflective coatings, prime lenses, the Canon EF-S 18-55mm and EF 50mm families, photographic-lens design, chromatic and spherical aberration, vignetting, flare, optical transfer and diffraction. Three community pages are only scoped examples: a detailed tracked and stacked Andromeda workflow, a first macro-lens picture without a controlled comparison and a moon image whose commenters still ask which camera and whether it is a composite. No captured source supplies a same-body, same-scene, output-normalized comparison of the six exact offers, verifies current condition or compatibility, establishes one universal price-to-sharpness cutoff or proves that premium glass, a cheap prime or the kit lens is automatically the right purchase.
generator_view.target: Audit what each frozen seller page, lens-family page, optical concept and community image can and cannot establish about upgrading the actual EOS 4000D and EF-S 18-55mm III baseline. Build an exact-offer table that separates price, aggregate, condition, bundle, warranty, mount, sensor-format fit, focal length, aperture, autofocus, stabilization and accessories from unresolved sample quality and current delivery. Explain prime-versus-zoom tradeoffs, coatings, chromatic and spherical aberration, vignetting, flare, scale-dependent OTF or MTF and diffraction without turning any label or price into a universal sharpness ranking. Keep the Andromeda, macro and moon examples tied to their capture, tracker, stack, processing, crop, output and missing metadata. Specify exact identity, compatibility, condition, decentering, focus, aperture, contact, accessory, warranty, return and delivered-cost checks. Design the smallest reversible same-body and same-operator trial for indoor family, moving children, portraits, travel, landscape and backlight, with matched field of view, perspective, framing, focus target, exposure and final web or small-print output. Track usable-frame rate and focus hits; then assess image-zone detail, tonal separation, lateral color, illumination falloff, stray-light behavior, subject separation, IS and AF behavior, portability, editing burden and finished-result preference as distinct observations. Predeclare meaningful-improvement, condition, compatibility, workflow, output and total-cost gates. End with the lowest-total-cost exact passing lens only when it meaningfully improves the declared outputs over the kit, or keep the kit, rent for a special task, save for another need, rerun a corrected comparison or defer.
